    - A tree's never just timber. It stood there before any of us, and it'll go to sea in a hull. The least I can do is say thank you.
    - I was twenty-three. A tree that had been judged a hundred times came down the wrong way, and a better cutter than me was under it. I was close enough to hear it crack and too far to do anything.
    - Since then I put a hand on every one and thank it before it falls. The young ones grin. None of them has ever seen me skip it. I don't tell many people that, *Player*.
    - Twice this year. End of winter, a cutting party came back to camp and found it torn apart, and every axe-handle bitten through.
    - This spring something large followed a crew through the trees all afternoon and never once showed itself. I called them all out before dark and I've not sent them back.
    - I don't know what it was, either time, and I'll not guess. I've not lost a cutter in twelve years. I mean to keep it so.
    - Torva says the old fox is done with, and Caddoc's traps hold. Good. That tells me nothing about my axe-handles, nor about what walked behind my crew. So we stay at the edge.
    - She wants deep-forest timber for the Gap Runner. Tall, close-grained, slow-grown. She's sure it's the length she keeps losing by.
    - Maybe she's right. I'll still not send a crew in for a keel. The quay hands can tell you the rest, they've heard us often enough.
    - She still wants her tree. But Jory tells me she's using the driftwood, every pin of it, and she's not said a word about that. From Tamsin, that's thanks.
    - Go careful. Keep where you can be heard.
